title: [bug] Factory post.doctor fails: stale agent.dcg check + gtbi.nightly --user timer not enabled
description:
After the fresh-host install chain fixes (gtbi-9z5 home ownership, gtbi-enr installed_check, gtbi-ar4 enable-linger), the QEMU factory install now COMPLETES end-to-end and ~50 doctor checks pass. The remaining Factory failure is post.doctor: it requires .summary.fail==0 AND .summary.warn==0 (tests/vm/test_factory_install_ubuntu.sh ~L483), and two WARN checks remain:

1. agent.dcg (scripts/lib/doctor.sh check_dcg ~L1993/2001): STALE — DCG was removed in the ecosystem cleanup, but doctor still probes for it and warns 'not installed (optional)'. Remove check_dcg + its call (and any agent.dcg references). Clear leftover bug.

2. gtbi.nightly: doctor check 'systemctl --user is-enabled gtbi-nightly-update.timer' warns because the --user timer is not enabled after install. enable-linger (gtbi-ar4) now creates /run/user/<uid>, but the gtbi.nightly install's 'systemctl --user enable' still isn't taking effect on the fresh host. Investigate how the install enables the --user timer as target_user (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/DBUS env, timing after linger) and ensure it actually enables so doctor reports pass.

## Acceptance
- gtbi doctor reports 0 fail / 0 warn on a fresh QEMU host (agent.dcg gone; gtbi.nightly enabled).
- Factory Installer E2E (Fresh Host/QEMU) green end-to-end (validate via workflow_dispatch).
- Docker installer matrix stays green (no systemd there — nightly/linger no-op gracefully).

Final link in the factory fresh-host chain (gtbi-9z5 -> gtbi-enr -> gtbi-ar4 -> this).
close_reason: Factory post.doctor now 0 fail / 0 warn (PR #45). Removed stale check_dcg + orphaned helper; nightly --user timer reliably enables via SYSTEMD_OFFLINE=1 busless enable (split from start, gated on systemd so Docker no-ops), SYSTEMD_OFFLINE in installed_check/verify. Validated: Factory Installer E2E (Fresh Host/QEMU) run 27505592500 = SUCCESS, green end-to-end. Fresh-host install chain (9z5 home -> enr packages -> ar4 linger -> z9s doctor) fully resolved.

title: [bug] loginctl enable-linger lost — headless --user nightly timer broken + /run/user missing
description:
## Symptom
Factory E2E (fresh host) post-install assertion fails: 'post.runtime_dir: /run/user/1000 missing'. (Install itself now completes after gtbi-9z5 + gtbi-enr.)

## Root cause
gtbi.nightly is a systemd '--user' timer (installed_check: 'systemctl --user is-enabled gtbi-nightly-update.timer'). A --user timer only runs without an active login session if the user is LINGERING (loginctl enable-linger), which also makes systemd create /run/user/<uid>. GTBI used to run 'loginctl enable-linger' (v0.2.0, commit fff59332) but it was removed in a6fab878 (Dicklesworthstone stack removal, PR #7). Now nothing enables linger -> on a headless host /run/user/<uid> never exists, 'systemctl --user enable' for the nightly timer can't work, and nightly auto-update is broken. The Docker CI matrix doesn't catch it (no systemd in containers).

## Fix
Restore 'loginctl enable-linger "$TARGET_USER"' in a root-run step of the user-setup path (scripts/lib/user.sh ensure_user, which runs as root). Must be NON-FATAL and guarded (skip if loginctl absent / no systemd) so the Docker test-installer matrix (no systemd) stays green. This creates /run/user/<uid> and makes the --user nightly timer work headless.

## Acceptance
- Factory E2E post.runtime_dir passes; gtbi.nightly --user timer enabled on a fresh headless host.
- Docker installer matrix stays green (enable-linger no-ops gracefully without systemd).
- Validate via Factory workflow_dispatch.

Related: gtbi-9z5, gtbi-enr (same factory fresh-host chain); regression from PR #7 (a6fab878).
close_reason: Restored loginctl enable-linger in ensure_user (PR #44, non-fatal/guarded; root). Fixes headless --user nightly timer + creates /run/user/<uid>. Validating via Factory workflow_dispatch.

title: [bug] base.system/cli.modern installed_check under-specifies apt bundle → packages skipped on fresh host (d8b regression)
description:
## Symptom
Factory E2E (fresh QEMU host) fails at lang.bun: 'error: unzip is required to install bun'. Install log shows 'Skipping base.system (already installed)'.

## Root cause
gtbi-d8b made the per-module installed_check load-bearing for install-skip (the generated install_<module> guard via gtbi_should_skip_module). Two modules install an apt BUNDLE but have an installed_check that only checks a SUBSET:
- base.system: check 'command -v curl && command -v git && command -v jq' but installs 'curl git ca-certificates unzip tar xz-utils jq build-essential gnupg lsb-release zstd'.
- cli.modern: check 'command -v rg && command -v tmux && command -v fzf' but installs 'ripgrep tmux fzf direnv jq gh git-lfs lsof dnsutils netcat-openbsd strace rsync sqlite3' (+ optional lsd/eza/bat).
On a host that already has the proxy tools (the QEMU cloud image has curl/git/jq), the guard skips the WHOLE module, so unzip/build-essential/zstd/gnupg (base) and sqlite3/gh/git-lfs/etc (cli) never install -> downstream failures (bun needs unzip; gastown needs sqlite3). Before d8b, generated modules had no install-time guard, so this never skipped on fresh installs.

## Fix
Make the installed_check for base.system and cli.modern represent the critical binaries they install (correct binary names: ripgrep->rg, dnsutils->dig, netcat-openbsd->nc, build-essential->gcc, gnupg->gpg, xz-utils->xz, git-lfs->git-lfs). Exclude optional (|| true) installs (lsd/eza/bat). Regenerate scripts. Audit other modules (single-package apt + verified_installer modules are 1:1 and fine).

## Acceptance
- Factory E2E fresh host gets past Language Runtimes (bun installs; unzip present).
- On a host with curl/git/jq, base.system is NOT skipped while unzip/build-essential/etc are missing.
- gtbi doctor accurately reports these modules; CI Gate + manifest drift green.
- Validate via Factory workflow_dispatch.

Related: gtbi-d8b (introduced the load-bearing guard), gtbi-9z5 (prior fresh-host fix).
close_reason: Fixed (PR #43): expanded base.system + cli.modern installed_check to represent their full apt bundles (unzip/xz/gcc/gpg/zstd; direnv/gh/git-lfs/lsof/dig/nc/strace/rsync/sqlite3). d8b's load-bearing per-module guard no longer skips them on hosts that merely have curl/git/jq, so unzip et al. install on fresh hosts. Drift clean; test_doctor_generated unchanged (2 pre-existing). Validating via Factory workflow_dispatch.

title: [bug] Fresh-host install fails: shell.omz can't mkdir ~/.oh-my-zsh (Permission denied)
description:
## Symptom
Factory Installer E2E (Fresh Host/QEMU) fails reproducibly (2 consecutive runs) at the shell_setup phase. Checksum verification PASSES ('✓ Verified: ohmyzsh') — the failure is a PERMISSIONS error:
  fatal: cannot mkdir /home/ubuntu/.oh-my-zsh: Permission denied
  Error: git clone of oh-my-zsh repo failed
  ERROR: shell.omz: verify_checksum or installer execution failed -> Phase 'Shell Setup' failed

## Context
- shell.omz (gtbi.manifest.yaml ~214) runs as target_user with verified_installer ohmyzsh (sh --unattended --keep-zshrc); oh-my-zsh's installer does 'git clone ... ~/.oh-my-zsh'.
- The QEMU factory is a FRESH host where the 'ubuntu' user does NOT exist before install (preflight logs 'ubuntu user does not exist before install') — GTBI creates it (users.ubuntu / base.filesystem phases).
- Running as ubuntu, mkdir in /home/ubuntu fails with Permission denied => /home/ubuntu is not owned/writable by ubuntu at shell_setup time on a fresh host.
- NOT reproduced by Installer CI Docker matrix (passes) — likely because those containers pre-provision the ubuntu user/home differently than a fresh cloud image. So this is a fresh-host-path bug the lighter CI doesn't catch.

## Likely root cause
Home-directory ownership/permissions for the installer-created target user: /home/ubuntu (or the home created during user/filesystem setup) is left root-owned (or not chowned to TARGET_USER) before the shell phase runs as that user. Investigate users.ubuntu / base.filesystem home creation + ownership (chown -R $TARGET_USER:$TARGET_USER $HOME), and whether useradd -m / home creation happened with correct ownership on a fresh host.

## Acceptance
- Factory Installer E2E (Fresh Host/QEMU) passes end-to-end (validate via workflow_dispatch).
- shell.omz installs as target_user on a fresh host (home writable by the user before shell phase).
- Add/keep a fresh-host assertion for target-home ownership.

## Note
Separate from gtbi-d19 (canary OBE DCG tests). Found while re-running the factory job to confirm a suspected flake — it is NOT a flake (reproducible, same shell.omz permission error both runs).
close_reason: Fixed (PR #42): ensure_user now guarantees the target user owns its home (user_ensure_home_owned: chown -R after both useradd and already-exists branches; path-guarded). Validated via Factory E2E workflow_dispatch (run 27503345278): shell_setup/shell.omz now PASSES on a fresh QEMU host (previously 'cannot mkdir ~/.oh-my-zsh: Permission denied'). The factory now progresses to a SEPARATE, distinct fresh-host failure (lang.bun needs unzip) tracked in a new issue.

title: [bug] Installer Canary red — OBE DCG/removed-tool assertions in VM canary harness
description:
## Symptom
Scheduled Installer Canary (Docker) + (Strict) fail on main. Root cause: tests/vm/test_runner.sh PHASE 2.6 runs tests/e2e/test_git_safety_guard_removal.sh, which asserts the install log + doctor MENTION DCG. DCG (and git_safety_guard) were removed in the ecosystem cleanup (#35/#28), so it fails: '[FAIL] [install_log_has_dcg] Install log does not mention DCG'. Not caught earlier because the canary runs only on schedule/workflow_dispatch, not in the CI Gate (Installer CI is green).

## Fix
- tests/vm/test_runner.sh PHASE 2.6 + tests/e2e/test_git_safety_guard_removal.sh: remove (DCG migration verification is OBE) OR rewrite to assert NEITHER git_safety_guard NOR DCG is present. Recommend removal of the PHASE + test since both tools are gone.
- Delete the orphaned DCG test suite: tests/vm/dcg_edge_case_tests.sh, dcg_functional_test.sh, dcg_integration_test.sh, dcg_pack_test.sh, dcg_performance_test.sh, dcg_slb_integration_test.sh, dcg_smoke_test.sh (DCG removed; verify not invoked elsewhere).
- Audit the rest of the canary/factory VM harness for other removed-tool assertions (agent-mail, swarm, cloud, ntm, cass, meta-skill): tests/vm/selection_checks.sh, tests/vm/test_install_artifacts.sh, tests/vm/test_gtbi_update.sh, tests/vm/test_runner.sh PHASE 3+, and any factory test. The canary fails fast at 2.6, so more failures may be hidden behind it.

## Validation (important)
The canary does NOT run on PRs (schedule + workflow_dispatch only). After merge, validate via 'gh workflow run "Installer Canary (Docker)"' (+ Strict) on main and confirm green end-to-end; iterate. Installer CI (lighter) will gate the PR but won't exercise the canary suite.

## Acceptance
- Installer Canary (Docker) + (Strict) green end-to-end on main (verified via workflow_dispatch).
- No removed-tool assertions remain in the VM/factory harness.
- CI Gate green on the PR.

Note: Factory Installer E2E (QEMU) failed separately on a transient oh-my-zsh git-clone flake (shell.omz) — being re-run to confirm; not part of this issue unless it recurs.
close_reason: Removed OBE DCG/git_safety_guard assertions from the canary harness (PR #41): deleted PHASE 2.6 + tests/e2e/test_git_safety_guard_removal.sh, the 7 tests/vm/dcg_*.sh files, and a stray test_dcg_update. Validated post-merge via workflow_dispatch: Installer Canary (Docker) run 27500879906 SUCCESS and (Strict) run 27500880385 SUCCESS — green end-to-end, no failures hidden behind 2.6.

title: [bug] Install resume is phase-level, not module-level — new modules skipped on upgrade
description:
## Repro (confirmed by user)
Install GTBI v0.2.0 (before Gastown existed), then re-run the latest installer. The 'stack' phase is already recorded complete in state.json, so install.sh's default --resume skips the ENTIRE stack phase -> the newly-added stack.gastown module never runs. Result: 'gt' is not installed, with no error shown. (Same happened class for gtbi-56q: user_setup/passwordless_sudo re-run skip.)

## Root cause
- install.sh always runs with --resume (install.sh ~L1161); resume skips any phase marked complete via state_should_skip_phase (scripts/lib/state.sh ~L1004). Idempotency is PHASE-level.
- The generated per-phase installers (e.g. install_stack_dolt/bd/gastown in scripts/generated/install_stack.sh) have NO per-module installed_check guard at runtime — a module only installs if its whole phase runs.
- The manifest DOES define installed_check per module (e.g. stack.gastown: 'command -v gt'), but it is consumed by doctor/selection, not by the install execution path.

## Fix: move idempotency to module-level
During resume, even for phases marked complete, evaluate each module's installed_check and install modules whose check fails (i.e. are missing). Concretely: emit a per-module installed_check short-circuit in the generated install_<module> functions (skip if present, install if absent), AND ensure resume still enters phases to run those per-module checks (or add a resume reconciliation pass that installs any manifest module whose installed_check fails). Generator change in packages/manifest/src/* + scripts/lib/*; regenerate scripts/generated/.

## Must preserve
- Fast resume: already-installed modules skip quickly via installed_check (no redundant downloads).
- Correct dependency ordering, dry-run support, and no re-running expensive completed work.
- --force-reinstall semantics unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- A v0.2.0 -> latest re-run installs newly-added modules (e.g. gastown) WITHOUT --force-reinstall or --only; 'gt' present and 'gtbi doctor' green afterward.
- Already-present modules are skipped via installed_check (verify no redundant re-download of dolt/bd).
- Add/extend an upgrade-path CI test (the E2E Upgrade and Repair job): record state with a module absent, then assert that module installs on resume.
- CI Gate green; manifest drift clean.

## Workaround (documented for users meanwhile)
bash install.sh --only stack.gastown --yes   # or --only-phase stack

## Related
gtbi-56q (closed) — same phase-skip class for identity.passwordless_sudo.
close_reason: Module-level install idempotency implemented (Option A, PR #38). Generator emits a per-module installed_check guard in each install_<module> (reuses gtbi_should_skip_module: respects run_as + GTBI_FORCE_REINSTALL; bypassed in dry-run). state_should_skip_phase now re-enters a completed phase when any of its modules is missing (via gtbi_module_is_installed; used install_helpers path since run_manifest_check_command/doctor_checks isn't sourced during install; defensive fallback to fast-resume). Proven by extended E2E Upgrade test (Phase 4): missing gt reinstalls on resume, present dolt/bd self-skip -> E2E Upgrade and Repair GREEN. Fixes the v0.2.0->latest upgrade gap that left Gastown uninstalled.

Renumber so agents->stack are contiguous and CONSISTENT with install.sh's current phases.
- scripts/lib/install_helpers.sh: cloud_db|cloud-db normalization (~L150).
- scripts/lib/rescue.sh: cloud_db phase mapping (~L318-319).
- scripts/lib/support.sh: cloud_db phase refs (~L1474-1475).
Verify install.sh phase numbering matches state.sh after. Regenerate if any generated script encodes phases. Verify: E2E resume-after-failure (CI), test_local_progress, rescue/state unit tests, bash -n. CI Gate green.

title: Require CI to pass before PR auto-merge (always-on CI Gate)
description:
Auto-merge currently squashes PRs immediately because main's branch protection has no required status checks. Add a single always-reporting 'CI Gate' required status check so auto-merge waits for Installer CI to pass.

Constraint: all PR workflows (installer.yml, checksum-system-tests.yml, toon-integration-tests.yml) use path filters. A naively-required path-filtered check blocks PRs that don't touch those paths (the check never reports). Solution: a 'CI Gate' that always reports — green when Installer CI passes OR is legitimately skipped, red when it fails — and require only that one context.

Must preserve direct-to-main commits for beads/docs (keep enforce_admins off; no required reviews / push restrictions).

Auto-merge now waits for CI; path-skipped PRs still pass via the changes-gated jobs + if:always() aggregator. Direct-to-main beads/docs commits preserved (admin bypass).

title: fix: dolt verified_installer runs as non-root user
description: The dolt installer (stack.dolt) has run_as: root in the manifest, but the code generator emits `| bash` instead of `| run_as_root_shell` for the verified_installer pipe. This causes dolt's install.sh to error: 'must run as root'. Root cause: generate.ts generateVerifiedInstallerSnippet() else-branch calls buildVerifiedInstallerPipe() which returns just 'bash'; the target_user case correctly uses run_as_target_runner but there's no equivalent for root. Fix: detect run_as === 'root' and emit run_as_root_shell as the pipe target, then regenerate scripts.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add PR-gated lightweight fresh-host install check (bare container)
description:
## Why
The Docker test-installer matrix masks fresh-host install bugs because it pre-installs prerequisites (unzip tar xz-utils gnupg) and pre-configures the ubuntu user/sudoers. As a result, a chain of real fresh-host bugs (gtbi-9z5 home ownership, gtbi-enr installed_check completeness, gtbi-ar4 linger, gtbi-z9s doctor) only got caught by the WEEKLY QEMU factory, not on PRs. Gating the full QEMU factory on PRs is impractical (~15 min, needs a KVM runner). Add a fast, lightweight bare-container fresh-host job to Installer CI so the install-blocking class is caught on every PR.

## Design
Add a new job to .github/workflows/installer.yml (so it's covered by the CI Gate) that simulates a fresh host and runs the installer:
- Container: a clean ubuntu image (match a matrix version, e.g. 24.04 or 25.10).
- Do NOT pre-install the bundle packages GTBI is responsible for (unzip, xz-utils, gnupg, build-essential, zstd, sqlite3, ripgrep, etc.). Pre-install ONLY the minimum to run the installer AND the 'proxy tools' curl+git+jq+ca-certificates+sudo — this specifically reproduces the condition that masked gtbi-enr (base.system installed_check proxy passing while the bundle is missing).
- Simulate the orphaned-home case for gtbi-9z5: create a root-owned /home/ubuntu (ubuntu user absent or removed without -r) so the installer must create/adopt+chown it.
- Run: GTBI_CI=true bash install.sh --yes --skip-preflight --skip-ubuntu-upgrade --mode vibe (mirror the existing matrix invocation).
- Assert (the regression guards): install exits 0; /home/ubuntu owned by ubuntu; key packages that were missing now present (unzip, sqlite3, gcc, zstd); stack tools installed (gt, bd, dolt) and bun/uv present.
- Do NOT require systemd/linger or doctor warn==0 here (Docker has no systemd; that stays the factory's job). Focus on the install-blocking fresh-host class.
- Wire the new job into the 'ci-gate' aggregate job's needs: list (so it gates auto-merge) and ensure it's covered by the 'changes' path filter (relevant=true on script/install changes).

## Acceptance
- New job runs on PRs, is part of CI Gate, and passes on current main.
- Reverting any of gtbi-9z5/gtbi-enr/gtbi-9z home fixes would make this job fail (i.e., it actually catches the class) — demonstrate the reasoning.
- Docker matrix + full CI stay green; QEMU factory remains on its weekly schedule for systemd/linger coverage.
- CI Gate green.

title: Configure Git and Dolt user identity (idempotent name/email prompt in installer)
description:
## Problem
The installer never configures Git user.name/user.email (only newproj.sh WARNS if missing) and never configures Dolt identity at all. Dolt requires user.name/user.email for commits just like Git — without them, Dolt/beads commits fail. Users currently have to set both manually.

## What to do
Add an IDEMPOTENT step to the installer that collects the user's full name + email once and configures BOTH Git and Dolt (per target user).

### Behavior
- Run as target_user (writes ~/.gitconfig and ~/.dolt/config_global.json).
- Placement: finalize phase (runs after stack.dolt is installed so 'dolt config' works). It's a finalize try_step, not a tool module.
- Idempotent:
  - If git has BOTH user.name+user.email AND dolt has BOTH -> skip silently.
  - If one tool has identity and the other doesn't -> copy the existing values across (no prompt).
  - If neither -> prompt (interactive) or use env override; else skip with a clear 'set later' message.
- Prompt only when interactive (TTY available and not YES_MODE/--yes). Reuse the gum_ui.sh /dev/tty pattern; add a gum text-input helper (gum_input) since only gum_confirm/gum_choose exist today. Fall back to 'read -r -p ... < /dev/tty' if gum unavailable.
- Non-interactive (--yes/vibe/no-TTY): use env overrides if provided (GTBI_GIT_NAME / GTBI_GIT_EMAIL; also honor GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL if set), otherwise skip with a log_warn telling the user how to set it later. Do NOT block a non-interactive install.
- Validate: non-empty name; email contains '@'. Re-prompt on invalid in interactive mode.
- Apply: git config --global user.name/user.email; dolt config --global --add user.name/user.email (verify exact dolt syntax; dolt is installed in dev env to check).

## Acceptance criteria
- Fresh interactive install prompts once; both 'git config --global user.name/email' and 'dolt config --global --get user.name/email' return the entered values afterward.
- Re-run / resume does NOT re-prompt when identity already configured (idempotent).
- Non-interactive install with GTBI_GIT_NAME/GTBI_GIT_EMAIL set configures both without prompting; without them, install completes with a warning (no hang).
- Unit test covers: skip-when-set, copy git<->dolt, env-override path, --yes/no-TTY skip, validation.
- 'gtbi doctor' optionally reports missing identity (nice-to-have).
- CI Gate green; manifest drift clean.

## References
- gum_ui.sh: gum_confirm/gum_choose + /dev/tty pattern (add gum_input).
- YES_MODE flag (install.sh:1198).
- newproj.sh:830 already checks git identity (can reuse/centralize the check).
close_reason: Added idempotent Git+Dolt identity config to the installer (PR #40, merged). New scripts/lib/identity.sh (configure_user_identity, sourced+called by finalize, runs as target_user): skip when both set, copy git<->dolt, env override (GTBI_GIT_NAME/EMAIL, GIT_AUTHOR_*), interactive gum_input prompt only with TTY && !YES_MODE, else warn+skip (never hangs). New gum_input helper in gum_ui.sh; test_identity.sh wired into Selection & Contract CI (7/7). Installer matrix 4/4 green (non-interactive path verified non-blocking).

title: [bug] gtbi doctor --fix does not handle identity.passwordless_sudo
description:
## Why this issue exists

`gtbi doctor` detects a failing `identity.passwordless_sudo` check and advises re-running the installer with `--mode vibe`, but `doctor --fix` had no handler for this check ID — it silently fell through to the unknown-check skip path.

The re-run advice itself is also broken: when the `user_setup` phase is already recorded as complete in the state file, a re-run skips that phase entirely and never calls `enable_passwordless_sudo`.

## What needs to be done

Add a `fix_passwordless_sudo` handler to `dispatch_fix` in `scripts/lib/doctor_fix.sh` that:
- Writes `/etc/sudoers.d/90-ubuntu-gtbi` with NOPASSWD for TARGET_USER
- Sets 440 permissions
- Validates with `visudo -c -f`
- Records the change for rollback

## Acceptance criteria
- `gtbi doctor --fix` repairs passwordless sudo without requiring a full reinstall
- Dry-run mode logs the planned action without writing anything
- Unit tests cover both cases
close_reason: Fixed in PR #18 (merged to main). Added fix_passwordless_sudo handler to dispatch_fix with dry-run support and 2 unit tests (67/67 pass).
